metaDescription: Five 28 inch two-stage snow blowers compared, battery and gas, on drive system, intake height, gear case construction, runtime and long-term ownership.
expertTake: The Honda HSS928 is our top pick because track drive, hydrostatic speed control and a commercial-grade engine suit steep, long driveways better than anything else here. The EGO SNT2807 is the pick for owners who want gas-class power with no fuel and who will accept battery runtime limits. If your driveway is short and flat, a 28 inch machine is more snow blower than you need, and a 24 inch model is easier to live with.
introParagraphs: A 28 inch two-stage snow blower is a serious machine for long driveways, big storms and owners who would rather make fewer passes. The extra width brings extra weight and a bigger storage footprint, so the question is whether the build underneath justifies it.

This guide explains how drive systems, gear cases and power sources differ at this size, and where battery and gas each make sense. The quick picks sit above, and the detailed reviews below show which machine suits which property.

products.name: Honda HSS928 28 in Track Drive Two-Stage Snow Blower
products.description:
The HSS928 uses a Honda GX270 commercial-grade overhead-valve engine, the type found in rental and professional equipment, and pairs it with a hydrostatic transmission. Hydrostatic means a hydraulic pump and motor replace belts and discs, so a single lever gives smooth, infinitely variable speed forward and reverse. That is a practical difference on a slope, where gear shifting wastes momentum.

Rubber tracks instead of wheels give grip on inclines and spread the machine's weight, which helps on ice and steep ground where wheels spin. Its 21.7 inch intake and 52 foot throw edge past the EGO's 21 inch intake, though the EGO throws farther at 60 feet. An auger height control lever sets the housing clearance for gravel or pavement.

Ownership benefits from a three-year residential warranty and arrival ready to run. Check oil and fuel before each use, use stabilized fuel and carry spare shear pins. The tradeoff is cost and weight, and it makes sense only on big or sloped driveways.
products.bestFor: Owners of long or sloped driveways who want track traction and a commercial-grade engine.
pros: Rubber tracks grip ice and slopes where wheels spin
Hydrostatic drive gives smooth, infinitely variable speed
Commercial-grade GX270 engine with wide parts support
Three-year residential warranty and no assembly needed
cons: Priced like premium equipment and heavy to store
Throw distance trails the EGO's 60 feet
Gas upkeep of fuel, oil and shear pins applies

products.name: EGO Power+ SNT2807 28 in Two-Stage Battery Snow Blower
products.description:
The SNT2807 draws power from two batteries at once, giving the motor higher current than one pack could provide. That is how a cordless machine reaches a 28 inch two-stage layout, with a variable speed steel auger and a self-propelled drive. The maker claims it can clear a 32-car driveway of 8 inches on a single charge, a bigger figure than the 24 inch EGO machines claim.

Its 60 foot throw is the longest here, beating the Honda's 52. A joystick controls 200 degree chute rotation and deflection, trigger-controlled steering helps with turns, and heated grips warm your hands. The bundled 12.0Ah batteries and dual-port charger make it a complete kit.

There is no engine to service, so nothing to winterize. The limit is runtime, and a long, heavy storm will test the packs. Store batteries indoors and charge them warm. It suits large driveways when you value quiet, simple ownership.
products.bestFor: Large driveway owners who want no-fuel ownership and the longest throw distance.
pros: Longest throw at up to 60 feet
Two 12.0Ah batteries and dual-port charger included
Joystick chute and heated grips for comfort
No engine, oil or fuel to maintain
cons: Runtime limits very long, deep snow sessions
Battery packs make it a premium purchase
Wheels lack the traction of Honda's tracks on ice

products.name: Ariens Professional 926083 28 in 420cc Two-Stage Snow Blower
products.description:
The Ariens Professional 926083 pairs a 420cc AX engine, the biggest displacement here, with a cast iron gear case. Cast iron absorbs shock far better than aluminum when the auger hits ice, which is why it is a mark of a machine meant for years of heavy use. Disc-O-Matic is Ariens's friction disc drive, which gives variable speed without a hydrostatic unit.

Auto-Turn triggerless steering lets the machine pivot without squeezing a trigger, a small but notable convenience for owners who find triggers tiring. The 420cc engine produces more torque than the Honda's GX270, though the Honda's tracks and hydrostatic drive give it an edge on slopes. Heated handgrips and electric start round out the comfort list.

Because the machine is a dealer-type product, parts and service are easy to find. Keep the friction disc clean, use stabilized fuel and check shear pins. It suits owners who want a long-service gas machine.
products.bestFor: Long-term owners who want cast iron durability and the largest engine in the group.
pros: 420cc AX engine is the largest displacement here
Cast iron gear case absorbs shock for longevity
Auto-Turn steering needs no trigger squeeze
Heated handgrips and electric start included
cons: Friction disc drive wears and needs adjustment over time
Heavier and more expensive than consumer-grade machines
Wheeled drive lacks the traction of Honda's tracks

products.name: EGO Power+ SNT2800 28 in Two-Stage Battery Snow Blower
products.description:
The SNT2800 is the same machine as the SNT2807 without the batteries or charger. It shares the 28 inch width, 21 inch intake and 60 foot throw, with a 200 degree chute joystick and heated grips. The 32-car claim assumes the 12.0Ah ARC batteries, which are sold separately.

It makes sense only if you already own compatible batteries, because the kit price difference can vanish once you buy two large packs. Compared with the Ariens Professional, you give up a gas engine's runtime but also its upkeep.

Store the batteries indoors and wipe snow off the housing after use. If you are starting from nothing, the SNT2807 kit is the simpler purchase.
products.bestFor: Existing EGO battery owners who need the 28 inch capacity without buying a second set of packs.
pros: Same 28 inch performance as the kit version
Up to 60 feet of throw with a joystick chute
Heated grips and trigger steering
Compatible with existing EGO ARC batteries
cons: Batteries and charger are not included
Capacity claim depends on buying two large 12Ah packs
Duplicates the SNT2807 for buyers without batteries

products.name: Ariens ST28DLE Deluxe 28 in Electric Start Gas Snow Blower
products.description:
The ST28DLE is a gas two-stage machine in Ariens's Deluxe line with a 28 inch width and electric start. The listing carries almost no technical detail, so unlike the Professional 926083 its engine size, gear case and drive details should be confirmed from the maker before buying.

Its value is brand and dealer support: Ariens has a long record in this category, and parts and service are widely available. As a mid-range alternative to the Professional line, it is the more affordable Ariens route.

As with any gas machine, use stabilized fuel, change oil each season and carry spare shear pins. Treat it as a candidate to confirm rather than a spec-proven pick.
products.bestFor: Ariens loyalists who want a mid-range 28 inch gas machine with dealer support.
pros: Established brand with wide dealer and parts support
28 inch two-stage width with electric start
Mid-range alternative to the Professional line
Gas runtime handles the longest storms
cons: Listing details on engine and drive are minimal
Needs fuel, oil and shear pin upkeep each season
Specs should be verified before purchase

buyingCriteria.criterion: Drive: tracks, wheels or friction disc
buyingCriteria.explanation: The drive decides traction and control. Tracks spread weight and grip ice and slopes, wheels are lighter and cheaper, and friction disc and hydrostatic transmissions differ in smoothness and wear. A common mistake is ignoring drive on a hilly driveway. The Honda HSS928 combines tracks and hydrostatic drive, while the Ariens Professional uses a Disc-O-Matic drive.

The gear case takes shock when the auger hits ice or a stuck pin breaks. Cast iron lasts longer than aluminum or plastic, and a bigger, commercial-grade engine lasts longer under load. The Ariens Professional pairs a 420cc engine with a cast iron case, and the Honda uses a GX270 engine.

A battery blower starts at a button but is capped by its packs, while gas runs until the tank is empty. At 28 inches, the EGO claims a 32-car driveway at 8 inches on two 12Ah packs. Deeper snow or longer driveways shorten that figure, so plan for the worst storm, not the average.

Intake height sets the deepest drift that fits, and throw sets how far snow lands from the path. The EGO has a 21 inch intake and 60 foot throw, the Honda a 21.7 inch intake and 52 foot throw. Wet snow throws much shorter than these best-case numbers.

At this size the machine is heavy, so steering matters. Triggerless and trigger-assisted steering both reduce the wrestling needed to turn. Heated grips make long sessions bearable. The Ariens Professional offers Auto-Turn, and the EGO offers trigger-controlled steering with a joystick chute.

A snow blower must work after months of idleness, so warranty and service matter. The Honda has a three-year residential warranty and the EGO has a five-year tool warranty on the SNT2425 platform. Dealer-backed brands like Ariens offer service and parts access.

specDecoder.meaning: A hydraulic pump and motor replace belts and discs, giving smooth variable speed in both directions.
specDecoder.watchFor: Only the Honda lists it here. Friction disc and variable drives wear over time.

specDecoder.meaning: A system that draws on two batteries at once so the motor gets more current than one pack allows.
specDecoder.watchFor: Capacity claims assume large 12Ah packs, so check what is in the box.

specDecoder.meaning: A claimed weight of snow moved each minute under ideal conditions.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Honda claims 1900, but wet snow reduces any figure sharply.

specDecoder.meaning: The cylinder volume swept, which correlates with torque at the auger.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Ariens 420cc is larger than the Honda GX270, but gear case and drive also decide performance.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drive and traction
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared tracks, wheels and drive type. The Honda's tracks and hydrostatic drive led for slopes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power source tradeoffs
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared gas runtime with battery convenience, using the EGO's 32-car claim and engine sizes of 420cc and the GX270.

howWeEvaluated.title: Build quality
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed gear case material, engine grade and warranty. The Ariens Professional's cast iron case and the Honda's commercial engine ranked highest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Control and comfort
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at steering, chute control and heated grips. Joystick chutes and triggerless steering added credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Data completeness

cards.label: Battery
cards.text: Quiet, instant start and no engine care, but runtime is capped by the packs. Includes the EGO SNT2807 and SNT2800.

cards.label: Gas
cards.text: Unlimited runtime and the best torque, but fuel, oil and shear pin upkeep apply. Includes the Honda HSS928, Ariens Professional 926083 and Ariens ST28DLE.

howToChoose.note: Pick battery for simple ownership on one large driveway and gas for very long storms or slopes.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Tracks or a pin-lock traction system, a hydrostatic or variable drive and enough torque to climb loaded.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Honda HSS928 with tracks and hydrostatic drive is the clear fit, with the Ariens Professional as a wheeled alternative.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a long or steep driveway. The Honda HSS928 and Ariens Professional 926083 reward it.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your driveway is moderate. The EGO SNT2807 or Ariens ST28DLE does the job without track drive.

maintenance.why: They protect the gearbox from jams. Spares avoid downtime in a storm.
Cold starts contaminate oil. Fresh oil protects the engine.
Ethanol gas gums the carburetor. Stabilizer or an empty tank prevents it.
Tracks and discs wear with use. Early replacement avoids a mid-winter failure.
Cold cuts capacity. Warm packs deliver full runtime.

faq.q: Is a 28 inch snow blower too big for a suburban driveway?
faq.a: On a short, flat driveway it is more machine than you need. It pays off on long or multi-car driveways where fewer passes save time.

faq.q: Is battery as powerful as gas at 28 inches?
faq.a: The EGO matches gas in clearing capacity for most snow. Runtime is the limit, so a long storm may need spare packs.
Tracks give better traction on slopes and ice and spread the weight. Wheels are lighter and turn more easily on flat ground.
A hydraulic pump and motor replace belts and discs, giving smooth variable speed in both directions with a single lever.

faq.q: Can I mix the EGO SNT2800 with other batteries?
faq.a: It uses EGO ARC 56V batteries, so you need that platform. Other brands are not compatible.

faq.q: How do I know the Ariens ST28DLE specs?
faq.a: The listing is sparse, so confirm engine size and drive details with the maker or a dealer before buying.
